title: Introducing yourself (Sich vorstellen)
summary: Say who you are and ask others: name, country, city, languages, job.
goals: Say your name, where you come from and where you live
Ask someone the same questions, politely (Sie) or to a friend (du)
Use heißen, kommen and wohnen in the present tense

points: Three ways to give your name: [[Ich heiße ...]], [[Ich bin ...]] (relaxed, among friends) and [[Mein Name ist ...]] (more formal). Your surname: [[Mein Familienname ist ...]]
Long words get easier when you split them: Familien-name.
Origin, home and languages: [[Ich komme aus ...]], [[Ich wohne in ...]], [[Ich spreche Deutsch und Englisch.]] You can also say [[Ich kann Deutsch und Englisch.]]
Age: [[Ich bin dreiundzwanzig Jahre alt.]] or just [[Ich bin dreiundzwanzig.]]
Jobs have a male and a female form, and there is no 'a' before them: [[Ich bin Student.]], [[Ich bin Studentin.]], [[Schüler]] / [[Schülerin]] (school pupil), [[Lehrer]] / [[Lehrerin]].
Family: [[Ich bin ledig.]] (single), [[Ich bin verheiratet.]] (married), [[Ich habe ein Kind.]], [[Ich habe zwei Kinder.]], [[Ich habe keine Kinder.]]
Hobbies: [[Meine Hobbys sind Fernsehen und Musik hören.]]

phrases.en: My hobbies are watching TV and listening to music.

notes.extra: Family status, children and hobbies ([[ledig]], [[verheiratet]], [[Kinder]], [[Hobbys]]), which forms often ask about.

videos.title: What a verb is: stem and ending

points: A verb describes an action, and the sentence is built around it: [[Ich spiele Fußball.]]
The infinitive, the form in the dictionary, is a stem plus an ending, and the ending is -en or just -n: [[lernen]] is lern + en. Learn every verb in this form.
In a sentence the verb is conjugated: its ending follows the subject. That depends on the person (I, you, he/she) and on singular or plural, so the personal pronouns decide it.
With [[du]], the ending is always -st: [[du lernst]], [[du kommst]].
Regular verbs (also called weak verbs) keep their stem: [[lernen]], [[machen]], [[spielen]], [[studieren]], [[arbeiten]].
Irregular verbs (strong verbs) change their stem in some forms, but take the same endings: [[sprechen]], [[du sprichst]]. Others: [[schlafen]], [[essen]], [[nehmen]], [[treffen]].

phrases.en: you speak (the stem changes: e to i)
regular verbs: to learn, do, play, study, work
irregular verbs: to sleep, eat, take, meet

points: In the present tense, a regular verb keeps its stem and adds an ending: [[ich]] -e, [[du]] -st, [[er]]/[[sie]]/[[es]] -t, [[wir]] -en, [[ihr]] -t, [[sie]]/[[Sie]] -en.
Three forms look like the infinitive, because they take -en: [[wir]], [[sie]] (they) and [[Sie]] (polite you).
Stem ending in s, ß or z: [[du]] adds only -t, because the s is already there: [[du reist]], [[du tanzt]].
Stem ending in d or t: add an extra e, so you can pronounce it: [[du arbeitest]], [[er arbeitet]], [[ihr arbeitet]]. Same with [[warten]] and [[antworten]].

sections.title: Three verbs to start with
sections.text:
To introduce yourself you need three verbs: [[heißen]] (to be called), [[kommen]] (to come) and [[wohnen]] (to live).

One rule builds the present tense of almost every verb: drop **-en** from the infinitive (the dictionary form, as on your word cards) to get the stem ([[wohnen]] minus -en = wohn-), then add the ending for the person: **ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en**. So [[ich wohne]], [[du wohnst]], [[er wohnt]]. The wir and sie/Sie forms look just like the infinitive. The few exceptions, like [[sein]] (lesson 3), get their own tables.

Three questions and their answers:
- [[Wie heißen Sie?]] - [[Ich heiße Hayk.]]
- [[Woher kommen Sie?]] - [[Ich komme aus Armenien.]]
- [[Wo wohnen Sie?]] - [[Ich wohne in München.]]

In every sentence the verb is the *second* part.

One trap: the stem of [[heißen]] already ends in ß, so the du form adds only **-t**: [[du heißt]], not 'heißst'.

items.de: Mein Vorname ist Hayk. Mein Nachname ist Tarkhanyan.
items.en: My first name is Hayk. My surname is Tarkhanyan.

items.de: Ich spreche Armenisch, Russisch und Englisch.
items.en: I speak Armenian, Russian and English.
What do you do for a living?

sections.title: heißen, kommen, wohnen in the present tense

sections.text:
Like Russian and Armenian, German changes the verb for each person: [[ich wohne]], [[du wohnst]] - я живу, ты живёшь - ես ապրում եմ, դու ապրում ես.

German also has two ways to say *you*, like Russian **ты / Вы** and Armenian **դու / Դուք**: [[du]] for friends, [[Sie]] (always with a capital S) for colleagues you don't know well.

Answer with the same verb as the question, then ask back: [[Woher kommen Sie?]] - [[Ich komme aus Armenien. Und Sie?]] With a friend: [[Und du?]] ([[Und dir?]] and [[Und Ihnen?]] from Unit 0 are only for [[Wie geht's?]].)
Write every noun with a capital letter: [[der Name]], [[das Land]], [[die Sprache]]. Country names too: [[Armenien]], [[Deutschland]].

items.en: What do you do for a living?

items.question: How do you ask a colleague's name politely?
items.explanation: Sie is the polite form; du is for friends.

items.instruction: Fill in the gaps: I come from Armenia and I live in Munich.
items.text: Ich ___ aus Armenien und ich ___ in München.
items.explanation: With ich the verb ends in -e: ich komme, ich wohne. Ich lebe in München is right too; wohnen is the everyday verb for where you live.

items.instruction: A new verb, same rule. Fill in the gap with lernen: He is learning German.
items.explanation: lernen minus -en = lern-, and er takes -t: er lernt. The same as er wohnt.
Question word first, then the verb, then Sie.

sections.title: Grammar words you'll hear in the videos
rows: nominative: the subject of the sentence
regular, irregular. The videos also call verbs like sprechen (du sprichst) irregular; this course says they change their vowel.
separable, inseparable (anrufen: ich rufe an; besuchen: ich besuche)
past participle (gemacht, gegangen); the videos say Partizip II
helping verb: haben or sein in the Perfekt
dative: after mit, zu, bei ..., and 'to whom' (dem, mir)
